note: Memory keys the server reads that are neither reserved nor under a system identity. A ratchet: the list may shrink and never grow silently. Every entry carries prose saying why the server does not act on this value; an empty reason fails the gate, and one that starts with UNREVIEWED counts as backlog rather than as a claim anyone has made.

migrateAppToolsKeysOnce() lists each owner's own `apps.*.tools` records to move one to the owner's own filename key, in the same namespace, with the value unchanged. The only thing it decides from them is the key name, and that comes from the owner's own app list (storage.getApp), never from the record. A forged record moves to a key the same owner could write anyway, and a record whose target key is taken or that has a live EXCHANGE listing is left where it is. Reviewed 2026-09-27.
appSellsForMoney() reads the app's own tools document (`apps.<filename>.tools`) through AppToolsDocSchema and asks one question of it: does any tool carry a currency price. The answer decides a RECOMMENDATION — which legal pages the details view says the app ought to have — and nothing the server enforces, pays or publishes. A principal who forges a money price into their own tools document gets told to write an imprint. User data the server only reads back, in the same shape app-tool-catalog.ts reads it.

UNREVIEWED. THIS IS A FINDING, left open on purpose. The keyed reads in this file are safe, because getMember and getMemberRow read NS_MEMBER, the literal string app-member, which carries no @ and so no principal can address it. listLapsed (src/services/app-members.ts:275) does not: it scans listAllMemory with prefix appmember. across EVERY namespace and returns the raw values. src/services/app-member-sweep.ts:49 then feeds those values to syncGrantsForMember with offeringIds empty, which revokes the EXCHANGE grants of the consumer named in the record, and to removeMember, which deletes the real roster row at NS_MEMBER/appmember.{slug}.{account}. Both targets come from the appId and owner fields of the scanned value, and the timer at src/server-bootstrap/service-init.ts:255 runs the sweep unattended. Any principal holding plain memory:write can therefore write appmember.{anything} into a namespace it already controls, with expiresAt in the past and a non-empty offerings array, and evict any member of any app while cancelling that member's grants. appmember. is not in RESERVED_OWNER_KEY_PREFIXES (src/utils/reserved-keys.ts:61) and no key-shape guard covers it. The fix is a code change in files this unit does not own: bind the scan to the system namespace, or reserve the prefix.

exempt.src/services/app-design-spec.ts:appdesig: The app's design spec: the builders' document beside the app. Read under NS_SPEC, the literal string app-design-spec, which carries no @ and so cannot be a GHII, GAII or GEAI - no principal can address that namespace through the memory API.
